newsitem.title: GERMANY: German not to face terrorism charges over ETA link.
newsitem.headline: German not to face terrorism charges over ETA link.

text.p: A German man detained in Germany and accused by Spain of aiding the violent Basque separatist group ETA will not face terrorism charges, prosecutors said on Friday.
Spanish authorities suspect Fritz Siemund of belonging to an ETA cell operating in the Spanish capital and believed to be behind several attacks in Madrid.

He was arrested in the German town of Wiesbaden on Monday at the request of Spanish police. They believe he was one of four people who fled on Saturday from an ETA safe house in Madrid, packed with weapons, shortly before an accidental explosion.
Public prosecutor Wolfgang Joerdens told a news conference Siemund was being investigated in connection with explosives offences on the basis of evidence provided by Spain.

But Joerdens said Siemund, who as a German citizen could not be extradited but could be tried here for serious offences committed abroad, could not face terrorism charges in his homeland because ETA did not operate in Germany.
"We have found no indications of ETA operating in groups in Germany," he told a news conference. "It is more on an individual basis."
Siemund could still face up to 10 years in prison if convicted of explosives offences.

Prosecutors said they were still searching for another German, Renate Heike Schubbert, a 33-year-old student from Wiesbaden who is the daughter of a mid-level Bundesbank (central bank) official. Spanish police believe Schubbert signed the rental contract for the safe house.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed about 800 people in a campaign of violence for an independent Basque state that has lasted almost 29 years.
Joerdens said Spanish authorities had said they found a canister inside the apartment with Siemund's fingerprints, about 80 kg (200 pounds) of explosives and a cache of weapons.
Siemund surrendered to police on Monday at a lawyer's office in Wiesbaden, west of Frankfurt.
